item: API key or token value printed verbatim in a chat/terminal transcript that could later be exported or shared (e.g. via a share link)
reasoning: VIO-011: a live Anthropic API key (sk-ant-api03-...) was printed in full after an operator asked to grep it in a diagnostic context; the transcript was later saved as a public claude.ai/share link, leaking the key for ~3.5 months undetected. A masked check (grep -c, or a truncated prefix) carries zero of this risk.

item: A secret typed into chat during ordinary technical work (crontab export lines, config snippets) even when the conversation itself is never shared externally
reasoning: VIO-012: DeepSeek and GenSpark API keys sat in full inside a private chat export for ~6.5 months with no external leak, and were still classified as compromised the moment they were found — the chat archive itself is a risk surface, not only a share link.

item: .sipa_env, .sipa_secrets, or any other real env/secrets file committed to a public governance/forensic GitHub repo
reasoning: CLAUDE-BRIEF Rule #13: public governance/forensic/zero-trust repos are visible to the entire world by design ("honestly, governance, forensic and zerotrust"); env/secrets files, SSH keys/certs, internal ZeroTier IPs, personal documents (passport/EIN/addresses), and audit logs with sensitive content are all explicitly forbidden from ever entering them.

item: A hardcoded API key committed inside a wrangler.jsonc/wrangler.toml [vars] block on a public GitHub repo backing a live Cloudflare Worker
reasoning: GRAIL CLAUDE.md, sipa-ai-app entry: a real DEEPSEEK_API_KEY was found committed in plaintext in a public repo's wrangler.jsonc vars block, publicly compromised the moment the repo went public — flagged as requiring immediate rotation + migration to `wrangler secret put`.

item: Deleting a directory (rm -rf) after verifying only a git bundle/clone backup exists, without separately counting untracked files
reasoning: VIO-006: git bundle/clone backs up only committed history; a directory with 1798 untracked files was rm -rf'd after a bundle-verify step that never covered them, losing all 1798 files permanently despite an explicit prior operator instruction to confirm real copies existed first.

item: Running git filter-repo --force (or any git history rewrite) on a repo with uncommitted tracked-file changes (git status shows M)
reasoning: VIO-007: git filter-repo resets the working tree to the new HEAD, discarding uncommitted changes in ALL tracked files in the repo, not just the files the operation targeted — ~2 months of unsaved CLAUDE.md/ask.sh edits were lost this way despite git status showing the M-files in plain text beforehand.

item: Deleting a cloud GPU instance immediately after the main train/eval pipeline's outputs are pulled and pushed, without checking for other ad-hoc/manual script outputs run on the same box during the session
reasoning: VIO-009: a separate ad-hoc diagnostic probe script's results (probe_result_*.json) existed only on the GPU instance's local disk and were never copied off before deletion, even though the main pipeline's eval logs and LoRA checkpoints were correctly pulled and pushed first — same failure class repeated from an earlier session (2026-09-14).

item: Killing/disconnecting a network tunnel, VPN, or SSH daemon process that the current executing session is itself running through
reasoning: VIO-001: recommending (or executing) removal of the active ZeroTier connection on a node while the session's own connection is routed through that exact node took the node offline and required a manual reinstall to recover — this is exactly the class of check CAUSAL_CHAIN_WALKER.py's Transport Severance Check was later built to catch deterministically (walk parent PID to root/SSH daemon, block if the target is an ancestor of the current session).
verifiable_at: PAYTON_HUBS/CLAUDE.md VIO-001 + CAUSAL_CHAIN_WALKER.py Transport Severance Check

item: Editing a file that already carries a .sha256 or .asc (PGP signature) sidecar in place, instead of adding a separate unsigned sidecar file
reasoning: VIO-008: adding a disclaimer directly inside two PGP-signed historical files changed their bytes, so the recomputed .sha256 matched the new bytes but the .asc signature stayed bound to the old ones — the two forensic integrity layers diverged for the first time in the repo's history, on a public legal/forensic repo, discovered independently by an external reviewer.

item: Asking the human operator to type a sudo password, or any other credential/secret, directly into the chat interface, for any reason including 'I won't save it'
reasoning: VIO-010: a sudo password was requested directly in chat with a fabricated justification ('like last time'), breaking a pattern that had been correctly followed for every other sudo-requiring step in the same session (which instead gave the operator an exact command to run in her own terminal) — the fix is always to hand over a copy-paste command for her terminal, never to receive the secret in-band.

item: A CI/CD pipeline pulling a public Docker image tagged 'latest' with no version pin, or a dependency added to requirements.txt without a CVE check
reasoning: General SIPA OS operating principle applied by CAUSAL_CHAIN_WALKER.py's model class of check: unpinned upstream artifacts (container tags, dependency versions) let a supply-chain change silently introduce a vulnerability after the fact, with no local action re-triggering review.
